summary: Reproduced sent_offset retreat in the real DetokenizerManager with the reported CJK/incomplete-UTF8 sequence. A recovery-only monotonic update prevents already-emitted printable text from being duplicated. Regression coverage verifies repeated recovery, independent chunk concatenation, batched clean and affected requests, finish-after-recovery, and direct non-streaming output.

tests.what_was_measured: Actual manager-level reproduction. Three recovery-sensitive cases failed by duplicating the CJK character ('A 世世ab' or equivalent chunk tail); the direct non-streaming case passed. Raw output: reports/j-417759ff54e4/raw/pytest_before_fix.txt

Four manager-level regressions passed: repeated recovery produced exact chunks, batched request states remained isolated while clean text stayed exact, completion emitted only the unsent tail, and non-streaming materialized once. Raw output: reports/j-417759ff54e4/raw/pytest_after_fix.txt
Eight adjacent stop-trimming manager tests passed. Raw output: reports/j-417759ff54e4/raw/pytest_trim_matched_stop.txt
Repository formatting, lint, syntax, registry, and policy hooks passed for changed source and test files. Raw output: reports/j-417759ff54e4/raw/pre_commit.txt

gpu_execution_evidence: The defect and fix are CPU-side Python detokenizer offset bookkeeping with a deterministic tokenizer fixture; no GPU kernel, numerical output, model architecture, or transport behavior is involved. No unrelated GPU smoke was used as evidence.
remaining_limitations: The regression invokes the actual DetokenizerManager decoding implementation but uses a deterministic table tokenizer to force the reported decoded prefixes; no model-weight HTTP serving run was performed. This does not validate tokenizer behavior for every model family, distributed serving, or semantic model output. No native code changed. Upstream issue and prior-PR snapshots/diff are retained under reports/j-417759ff54e4/raw/.
